clue.text: Priest tells senior clergy

parts.note: to tell a story is to relate it, so tells gives relates

explanation.surface: A priest passes on gossip to the bishops above him.
explanation.definitionFit: Bishops and archbishops are high-ranking churchmen, the senior ranks of the clergy.

clue.text: Entertain man having got beer

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, short for Reginald
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone is entertained by a fellow who has fetched a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale guests is to treat them lavishly or amuse them with stories, a synonym of entertain.

clue.text: The unordained could be found in Italy

indicators.note: the letters of the next word could be found rearranged inside it, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Ordinary churchgoers who are not priests might be met in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be found in' looks like a hidden-word signal, but the five letters of Italy are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Church members who are not clergy are lay people, collectively the unordained.

clue.text: Male player in band putting off one other player

parts.note: Tim is a male name, standing here for any man

indicators.note: putting off means sending away, so the letter for one is dropped from the musician

parts.note: a pianist is another kind of musical player
one is I as the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A man in a band drives out a rival musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male' seems to describe the player, but it gives the name TIM; PIANIST loses its I (one) to leave PANIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer playing kettledrums in an orchestra or band is a musician in that group.

clue.text: Outstanding foreigner resides in street

indicators.note: to reside in a place is to live inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner, a person from another country

explanation.surface: A remarkable immigrant lives on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient point is prominent or striking, one that stands out.

clue.text: Conclusion drawn from questionnaires ultimately

indicators.note: drawn from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A finding is reached by studying survey forms at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome or end product of a process is its conclusion.

clue.text: Scare female away, being honest

indicators.note: sending the female away means her letter is removed from the word for scare

parts.note: a fright is a scare

explanation.surface: Being truthful, someone drives off a woman with a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Right in the sense of just, fair and upright fits honest dealing.

clue.text: Act like a trouper or a trooper?

definitions.text: Act like a trouper or a trooper?

parts.words: Act like a trouper or a trooper?
parts.note: a trouper keeps going through hardship, and a trooper is literally a fighting man pressing on

explanation.definitionFit: To persevere doggedly in spite of difficulty, as a trouper does, while a trooper is literally a soldier.

clue.text: Lecturer is with number meeting the queen, one having audience

parts.note: taken as written
ten is a number
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A lecturer and a group of ten meet the monarch, who grants them an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one having audience' sounds like a royal audience, but it means someone who hears.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who hears or attends to sounds is part of an audience in the sense of hearing.

clue.text: Fancy images discriminating against the old

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: Elaborate pictures show bias against elderly people.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudice on grounds of years lived, especially against older people, is this form of bias.

clue.text: Member with a rota is one to go by the book

definitions.text: one to go by the book

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: A club member armed with a duty roster sticks rigidly to the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler for the strict letter of law or rules follows everything by the book.

clue.text: Fun-loving companion rested on floor covering in gym

indicators.note: in places the rested-on-covering pieces inside the letters for gym

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
lay is the past tense of lie, meaning rested
a mat covers part of a floor

explanation.surface: A playful friend lay on a mat in the gymnasium.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend to play games with, especially a child's partner in fun.

clue.text: Worked a short time, given lubrication

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
something given lubrication has been oiled

explanation.surface: A machine ran briefly once it had been greased.
explanation.definitionFit: To have laboured hard is to have worked.

clue.text: A fit adherent though curiously timid

indicators.note: curiously, meaning in an odd way, tells us to arrange these letters strangely

explanation.surface: A healthy supporter who is oddly lacking in courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking courage, fearful, cowardly in spirit: a synonym of timid.

clue.text: Engendering big explosive band

parts.note: fat means big or stout
HE is high explosive
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A huge bomb produces a band of debris.
explanation.definitionFit: To father offspring is to beget or engender them, so fathering means engendering.

clue.text: Singer blasted out in a hi-fi dept

indicators.note: blasted out suggests sound and letters thrown about, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A singer's songs boom from a stereo in a department store.
explanation.walkthrough: EDITH PIAF was a famous French chanteuse.
explanation.definitionFit: The French chanteuse known as the Little Sparrow was a celebrated vocalist.

clue.text: Cricketer in a terrible riot — it's slaughter there!

indicators.note: in places the cricketer inside the other pieces
terrible suggests disorder, so the following word is jumbled

parts.note: a bat is a batsman, a cricketer

explanation.surface: A cricketer caught up in an awful riot finds carnage.
explanation.walkthrough: TOIR is the anagram of riot made by 'terrible'; BAT (a batsman in cricket) goes inside A + TOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse is the place where animals are killed for meat.

clue.text: Medical specialist — is certain to get involved around start of birth?

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go around the start of birth
letters that get involved are mixed up together, an anagram signal
start of takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A specialist doctor is sure to be busy as a baby's delivery begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get involved' rearranges IS CERTAIN TO to OSTETRICIAN, and 'around' puts that round B, the 'start of birth'.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who specialises in childbirth and pregnancy care is a medical specialist.

clue.text: To sum up : you don't get this particular answer thus!

definitions.meaning: used to introduce a brief summary, briefly put

definitions.text: you don't get this particular answer thus
definitions.meaning: the answer has more than one word, so it cannot be given as just one

explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning briefly or in summary, and wryly also this answer's length being more than one single word.

clue.text: Farmhouse plus buildings and good area of land

parts.note: a range is a tract of grazing land

explanation.surface: A farm with its outbuildings, good pasture and wide acres.
explanation.definitionFit: A country house with its attached farm buildings is a farmstead of this kind.

clue.text: Army brought back females in foreign capital

indicators.note: brought back means the letters for the army are turned to run backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
hens are female birds

explanation.surface: Soldiers return with women in an overseas city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek capital is a capital city abroad from the British setter's view.

clue.text: Suggestive picture in the back bits of serious weekly

indicators.note: in puts the picture inside the selected letters
the back bits are the final letters of each word

parts.note: pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: A racy photo appears in the rear pages of a sober magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy or risqué material is spicy, suggestive in a sexual way.

clue.text: A goal finally by poor performer! Support palace!

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting actor
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A last-minute goal by a weak player, and fans cheer on Palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests football (Crystal Palace is a London club), but 'palace' is the Moorish palace in Granada.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Moorish citadel and royal residence in Granada, Spain, is a palace.

clue.text: Space set up around middle of factory for machine

indicators.note: around wraps the turned word round the middle letter
in a down clue set up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: room means space

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A space is arranged around a factory floor for a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns ROOM into MOOR, which goes 'around' T, the middle of factory.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that produces motion is a machine.

clue.text: Trouble with oil — topic for someone at Westminster?

indicators.note: trouble as a verb means to disturb, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A problem with oil is a hot subject for MPs.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster is the seat of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician, especially a career one, is found at Parliament in Westminster.

clue.text: At home nurse becomes mean

parts.note: in means at home
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: Caring for someone at home turns a person unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to plan or intend it.

clue.text: Good man restraining gee-gee that's dazed

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the horse goes inside the man

parts.note: Roy is a man's name
GG is short for gee-gee, a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A kind fellow holds back a stunned horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsteady and confused, groggy describes someone dazed.

clue.text: Delayed agent's return and blundered

indicators.note: return means the word for agent is read backwards

parts.note: a Fed is an American federal agent
erred means made a mistake, blundered

explanation.surface: An agent comes back late after making a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Put off until later, postponed, so delayed.
